name: Midface / cheek filler for tear trough

lead: Midface or malar filler adds volume to the cheek. Proponents say that restoring cheek support can reduce the look of an under-eye hollow without injecting the thin eyelid skin directly, which is why it is discussed as an alternative approach.

Hyaluronic acid midface filler has been studied for cheek augmentation in its own right, including a systematic review and several registered trials. Trials aimed at the tear trough via the cheek were not found.

paras: Filler adds volume to the cheek, which proponents say raises soft-tissue support and changes how light and shadow fall under the eye.

Fillers can cause bruising, swelling, lumps, and rarely vascular events including vision loss. A ten-year postmarket surveillance of a cheek filler examined delayed complications. Hyaluronic acid fillers can be dissolved with hyaluronidase, while calcium hydroxyapatite fillers are harder to remove.

lead: Midface or cheek filler is the injection of a dermal filler, most often hyaluronic acid (HA), into the malar area to restore volume.[1][2] In looksmaxxing discussions it is raised as a way to improve under-eye appearance by supporting the area from the cheek rather than treating the tear trough directly.[3]

A 2021 systematic review evaluated outcomes, safety and techniques of HA fillers for malar augmentation.[4] Postmarket surveillance of a flexible cheek filler has examined delayed complications over ten years.[5] The wiki found no trial designed specifically to treat the tear trough through cheek filler.

paras: Fillers are injected mainly to change facial appearance, including restoring volume lost with age and enhancing the cheeks.[2] HA is the most common filler material, and effects are generally described as lasting months, varying with product and provider.[2]

Common effects include bruising, redness, pain and itching; rarer ones include infection, lumps and allergic reaction, and very rarely blindness from embolization.[2] A study of calcium hydroxyapatite (Radiesse) notes that it is semipermanent and, unlike some HA fillers, cannot easily be dissolved, and describes a technique to remove excess product.[6]

A 2021 systematic review covers HA midface augmentation outcomes and safety.[4] Registered trials include an HA filler for cheek flattening (NCT01225354, n=20), a mid-face volume trial (NCT07126912, n=30, recruiting), an 80-person trial of dermal fillers including mid-face (NCT07160777) and a 232-person trial of HA fillers (NCT04647513).[7][8][9][10] None is registered as a tear-trough study.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, cheek filler appears in plans that combine several procedures, with posters saying cheek volume would raise the cheeks and increase under-eye support.[11]

claims.claim: Cheek filler gives the under-eye area more support.
